_readme: Single source of every number drawn in webpage/assets/*.svg and the table views in webpage/index.html.
Edit the values here, then run: python3 -I webpage/charts/make_charts.py
Times are seconds; null means 'not measured' and is drawn as 'pending'. Every value, with its conditions, is in docs/benchmarks.md.
rh_timelapse takes its three totals from rh_stages; seconds_per_hour is its playback rate when make_charts.py animates (ANIMATE = True).

rh_timelapse.title: Time to a verified Riemann Hypothesis proof
rh_timelapse.subtitle: Build, export and judge from sources on server A (384 threads), Lean 4.33.1; linear time axis.
rh_timelapse.source: (b) kernel replay only, no statement or axiom check. Official build: lean per module. Source: docs/benchmarks.md

rh_stages.title: Riemann Hypothesis proof: time per stage, official tools and Light-Prover
subtitle: 175,187 modules, Lean 4.33.1; server A, 384 threads; log scale. Light-Prover: --preset sound,
median of 3 runs on a pre-release snapshot with the same judge binaries as v0.1.
Official: one run per row.
source: (a) unmodified lake comparator, default settings (Lean-only configuration), shared server. (b) official
leanchecker with MIMALLOC_GENERIC_COLLECT=1000000: kernel replay only, no statement / axiom comparison.
Build: lean per module under a direct scheduler, a proxy for lake build. The Light-Prover total includes
about 12 s of preflight and preparation. Source: docs/benchmarks.md

judge.title: Judging the 61.6 GB Riemann Hypothesis export
subtitle: Light-Prover judge only, one run per row unless noted. The proof was ACCEPTED on every row;
four mutated exports were REJECTED on each machine and by the low-memory judge.
Official: lake comparator 52.7 h; leanchecker with one allocator setting 13.2 h (kernel only).
source: Memory-limited rows: cgroup limit, swap off. The first 128 GB run ran beside its four mutant checks;
the second 128 GB run and the 64 GB run ran alongside other runs. Machine C shared and memory-contended in
both runs (the first spent 404.2 s in the parse). Source: docs/benchmarks.md

rows.name: server A, 32 threads
rows.detail: low-memory judge, 128 GB, with mutant checks

projects.title: Official time / Light-Prover time, other projects
subtitle: End to end from sources, 6-100 CPUs per flow, both flows on the same CPUs, dependencies prebuilt,
one run each unless noted; log scale around 1x. Below 1x Light-Prover was slower.
Same verdicts on every row.
source: * Light-Prover on the released package (two runs, the first shown); official time from an earlier
